patterns.content: List comprehension replaces explicit for-loop append. [x*2 for x in items] is idiomatic Python; avoid result=[]; for x in items: result.append(x*2).
Use dataclasses or Pydantic instead of plain dicts for structured data. @dataclass class User: name: str; age: int — gives free __init__, __repr__, __eq__.
Context managers (with statement) replace try/finally for resource cleanup. with open(path) as f: body — file always closed even on exception.
Type hints on all function signatures: def process(items: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]. Use from __future__ import annotations for forward refs.
Prefer pathlib.Path over os.path. Path('data') / 'file.txt' instead of os.path.join('data', 'file.txt'). Use path.read_text() and path.write_text().
Exception handling: catch specific exceptions, not bare except. except ValueError as e: is correct; except Exception: is acceptable; bare except: is wrong.
f-strings for formatting: f'Hello {name}' instead of 'Hello %s' % name or 'Hello {}'.format(name). Multiline: f'result={value!r}'.
Dict/set comprehensions: {k: v for k, v in pairs} and {x for x in items if x > 0}. Use dict.get(key, default) instead of checking key in dict then accessing.
Use enumerate() and zip() instead of range(len()). for i, item in enumerate(items) instead of for i in range(len(items)): item = items[i].
Generator expressions for lazy evaluation: sum(x*x for x in range(1000)) is more memory-efficient than sum([x*x for x in range(1000)]).
